\section{Introduction}

Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) requires identifying semantic relations between entity pairs across multiple sentences, a task where encoder-based methods such as \citet{zhou2021atlop} long dominated.
Recent LLM-based approaches have closed this gap: \citet{wan2024genres} recast DocRE as constrained generation, \citet{xu2024lmrc} frame it as multi-choice reading comprehension, and \citet{chen2025docksrag} combine retrieval-augmented generation with structured knowledge.
These methods approach or surpass encoder baselines on DocRED \citep{yao2019docred} and Re-DocRED \citep{tan2022redocred} in extraction accuracy.
Yet every one of them outputs bare relation triplets $(e_h, r, e_t)$ without any indication of \emph{which sentences} in the document support each prediction.
In deployment contexts where predictions feed into clinical knowledge bases, legal due-diligence pipelines, or financial compliance systems, end users cannot verify a prediction without manually locating its textual basis across a multi-page document.

The absence of verifiable evidence creates a practical bottleneck.
Relation extraction outputs are consumed downstream by knowledge graph construction and human decision workflows.
When a system predicts that a drug interacts with a gene, or that a contract clause implies a liability, practitioners must trace each prediction back to source text before acting on it.
Without machine-generated evidence, this verification requires exhaustive manual review of the input document for every predicted relation.
Encoder-based methods have partially addressed this need: \citet{xiao2022sais} introduce sentence-level evidence supervision as an auxiliary signal, and \citet{ma2023dreeam} extend this with dynamic evidence retrieval through memory attention.
Both improve extraction quality \emph{and} produce evidence annotations.
However, encoder methods now trail LLM-based approaches in extraction accuracy, and their evidence mechanisms (binary sentence classification) do not transfer to generative architectures.
The community therefore faces a gap: the most accurate extractors provide no evidence, while the evidence-capable methods are no longer competitive.

This gap reflects a deeper structural difference between evidence in encoder and generative frameworks.
In SAIS and DREEAM, evidence retrieval is a binary classification task (does sentence $s_i$ support relation $r$?) that serves as auxiliary supervision.
The evidence signal \emph{regularizes} the encoder and improves extraction.
In LLM-based DocRE, evidence-grounded extraction requires the model to \emph{generate} complete evidence sentences as part of its output sequence, substantially increasing output length and decoding complexity.
Evidence production in this setting is not an auxiliary signal but an additional generation burden that competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
The fundamental asymmetry is clear: encoder evidence helps extraction; generative evidence costs extraction capacity.
This distinction motivates a systematic investigation of how to produce faithful evidence within LLM-based DocRE without sacrificing the extraction gains that make these models attractive.

We formalize evidence-grounded DocRE as a structured generation task for LLMs and conduct a systematic comparison of three post-training optimization paradigms: online reinforcement learning via GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath}, offline preference optimization via DPO \citep{rafailov2023direct}, and offline reinforcement learning via Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT, building on STaR \citep{zelikman2022star}).
Our experiments across 85+ configurations, spanning four model scales (1.7B to 8B), two model families, and two datasets, reveal three principal findings.
\textbf{First}, we identify a \emph{decoupling spectrum}: the strength of RL optimization pressure correlates with the severity of evidence-extraction decoupling.
GRPO with QLoRA \citep{hu2022lora} produces catastrophic decoupling where extraction accuracy collapses to near zero; GRPO with full-precision training shows mild decoupling; DPO exhibits gradual degradation; and RSFT maintains stable joint performance.
QLoRA acts as a catastrophic amplifier of the underlying optimization conflict rather than its root cause.
\textbf{Second}, we discover a \emph{scale-dependent evidence tax}: the cost of jointly producing evidence and relations follows a non-monotonic pattern across model scales.
At 1.7B parameters, evidence generation provides an implicit regularization benefit of +8 percentage points (pp) in Ign-F1; at 4B, it imposes a $-$7.5pp penalty; at 8B, the tax approaches zero.
This non-linear pattern overturns the naive assumption that evidence generation uniformly harms extraction.
\textbf{Third}, RSFT with NLI-based Contrastive Evidence Discrimination (CED) scoring emerges as the only effective optimization route.
By selecting high-quality training samples through output filtering rather than applying gradient-based optimization pressure, RSFT sidesteps the multi-objective competition that destabilizes RL and preference methods.

Our contributions are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item We formalize \textbf{evidence-grounded document-level relation extraction} as a generation task for LLMs, defining structured output formats that jointly produce relation triplets and their supporting evidence sentences.

    \item We characterize a \textbf{decoupling spectrum} across optimization paradigms: RL optimization pressure correlates with evidence-extraction decoupling severity (GRPO catastrophic $\rightarrow$ DPO gradual $\rightarrow$ RSFT none). We introduce the EDCR diagnostic metric, which captures this relationship with method-level $\rho = -0.965$.

    \item We identify a \textbf{scale-dependent evidence tax}: a non-monotonic cost pattern across 1.7B, 4B, and 8B parameters that overturns the assumption that evidence production uniformly degrades extraction quality.

    \item We establish \textbf{RSFT with NLI-based CED scoring} as an effective solution, achieving +4.92pp Ign-F1 over SFT at 4B scale. Our 1.7B RSFT model (50.50 Ign-F1) matches 8B SFT performance (50.51), enabling deployment-efficient evidence-grounded extraction at reduced computational cost.

    \item We present a \textbf{comprehensive empirical study} spanning 85+ experiments across four model scales, two model families, two datasets (DocRED, Re-DocRED), and three optimization paradigms, providing the first systematic analysis of evidence production in generative DocRE.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Introduction}

Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) requires identifying semantic relations between entity pairs across multiple sentences, a task where encoder-based methods such as \citet{zhou2021atlop} long dominated.
Recent LLM-based approaches have closed this gap: \citet{wan2024genres} recast DocRE as constrained generation, \citet{xu2024lmrc} frame it as multi-choice reading comprehension, and \citet{chen2025docksrag} combine retrieval-augmented generation with structured knowledge.
These methods approach or surpass encoder baselines on DocRED \citep{yao2019docred} and Re-DocRED \citep{tan2022redocred} in extraction accuracy.
Yet every one of them outputs bare relation triplets $(e_h, r, e_t)$ without any indication of \emph{which sentences} in the document support each prediction.
In deployment contexts where predictions feed into clinical knowledge bases, legal due-diligence pipelines, or financial compliance systems, end users cannot verify a prediction without manually locating its textual basis across a multi-page document.

The absence of verifiable evidence creates a practical bottleneck.
Relation extraction outputs are consumed downstream by knowledge graph construction and human decision workflows.
When a system predicts that a drug interacts with a gene, or that a contract clause implies a liability, practitioners must trace each prediction back to source text before acting on it.
Without machine-generated evidence, this verification requires exhaustive manual review of the input document for every predicted relation.
Encoder-based methods have partially addressed this need: \citet{xiao2022sais} introduce sentence-level evidence supervision as an auxiliary signal, and \citet{ma2023dreeam} extend this with dynamic evidence retrieval through memory attention.
Both improve extraction quality \emph{and} produce evidence annotations.
However, encoder methods now trail LLM-based approaches in extraction accuracy, and their evidence mechanisms (binary sentence classification) do not transfer to generative architectures.
The community therefore faces a gap: the most accurate extractors provide no evidence, while the evidence-capable methods are no longer competitive.

This gap reflects a deeper structural difference between evidence in encoder and generative frameworks.
In SAIS and DREEAM, evidence retrieval is a binary classification task (does sentence $s_i$ support relation $r$?) that serves as auxiliary supervision.
The evidence signal \emph{regularizes} the encoder and improves extraction.
In LLM-based DocRE, evidence-grounded extraction requires the model to \emph{generate} complete evidence sentences as part of its output sequence, substantially increasing output length and decoding complexity.
Evidence production in this setting is not an auxiliary signal but an additional generation burden that competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
The fundamental asymmetry is clear: encoder evidence helps extraction; generative evidence costs extraction capacity.
This distinction motivates a systematic investigation of how to produce faithful evidence within LLM-based DocRE without sacrificing the extraction gains that make these models attractive.

We formalize evidence-grounded DocRE as a structured generation task for LLMs and conduct a systematic comparison of three post-training optimization paradigms: online reinforcement learning via GRPO \citep{shao2024deepseekmath}, offline preference optimization via DPO \citep{rafailov2023direct}, and offline reinforcement learning via Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT, building on STaR \citep{zelikman2022star}).
Our experiments across 85+ configurations, spanning four model scales (1.7B to 8B), two model families, and two datasets, reveal three principal findings.
\textbf{First}, we identify a \emph{decoupling spectrum}: the strength of RL optimization pressure correlates with the severity of evidence-extraction decoupling.
GRPO with QLoRA \citep{hu2022lora} produces catastrophic decoupling where extraction accuracy collapses to near zero; GRPO with full-precision training shows mild decoupling; DPO exhibits gradual degradation; and RSFT maintains stable joint performance.
QLoRA acts as a catastrophic amplifier of the underlying optimization conflict rather than its root cause.
\textbf{Second}, we discover a \emph{scale-dependent evidence tax}: the cost of jointly producing evidence and relations follows a non-monotonic pattern across model scales.
At 1.7B parameters, evidence generation provides an implicit regularization benefit of +8 percentage points (pp) in Ign-F1; at 4B, it imposes a $-$7.5pp penalty; at 8B, the tax approaches zero.
This non-linear pattern overturns the naive assumption that evidence generation uniformly harms extraction.
\textbf{Third}, RSFT with NLI-based Contrastive Evidence Discrimination (CED) scoring emerges as the only effective optimization route.
By selecting high-quality training samples through output filtering rather than applying gradient-based optimization pressure, RSFT sidesteps the multi-objective competition that destabilizes RL and preference methods.

Our contributions are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item We formalize \textbf{evidence-grounded document-level relation extraction} as a generation task for LLMs, defining structured output formats that jointly produce relation triplets and their supporting evidence sentences.

    \item We characterize a \textbf{decoupling spectrum} across optimization paradigms: RL optimization pressure correlates with evidence-extraction decoupling severity (GRPO catastrophic $\rightarrow$ DPO gradual $\rightarrow$ RSFT none). We introduce the EDCR diagnostic metric, which captures this relationship with method-level $\rho = -0.965$.

    \item We identify a \textbf{scale-dependent evidence tax}: a non-monotonic cost pattern across 1.7B, 4B, and 8B parameters that overturns the assumption that evidence production uniformly degrades extraction quality.

    \item We establish \textbf{RSFT with NLI-based CED scoring} as an effective solution, achieving +5.38pp Ign-F1 over SFT at 4B scale (best seed). Our 1.7B RSFT model (50.50 Ign-F1) matches 8B SFT performance (50.51), enabling deployment-efficient evidence-grounded extraction at reduced computational cost.

    \item We present a \textbf{comprehensive empirical study} spanning 85+ experiments across four model scales, two model families, two datasets (DocRED, Re-DocRED), and three optimization paradigms, providing the first systematic analysis of evidence production in generative DocRE.
\end{enumerate}

Encoder-based methods have partially addressed this need: \citet{xiao2022sais} introduce sentence-level evidence supervision as an auxiliary signal, and \citet{ma2023dreeam} extend this with dynamic evidence retrieval through memory attention.
Both improve extraction quality \emph{and} produce evidence annotations.

The community therefore faces a gap: the most accurate extractors provide no evidence, while the evidence-capable methods are no longer competitive.

This gap reflects a deeper structural difference between evidence in encoder and generative frameworks.
In SAIS and DREEAM, evidence retrieval is a binary classification task (does sentence $s_i$ support relation $r$?) that serves as auxiliary supervision.
The evidence signal \emph{regularizes} the encoder and improves extraction.
In LLM-based DocRE, evidence-grounded extraction requires the model to \emph{generate} complete evidence sentences as part of its output sequence, substantially increasing output length and decoding complexity.
Evidence production in this setting is not an auxiliary signal but an additional generation burden that competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
The fundamental asymmetry is clear: encoder evidence helps extraction; generative evidence costs extraction capacity.
This distinction motivates a systematic investigation of how to produce faithful evidence within LLM-based DocRE without sacrificing the extraction gains that make these models attractive.

\textbf{Second}, we discover a \emph{scale-dependent evidence tax}: the cost of jointly producing evidence and relations follows a non-monotonic pattern across model scales.

\textbf{Third}, RSFT with NLI-based Contrastive Evidence Discrimination (CED) scoring emerges as the only effective optimization route.

\section{Introduction}

These methods approach or surpass encoder baselines on DocRED \citep{yao2019docred} and Re-DocRED \citep{tan2022redocred} in extraction accuracy.
Yet every one of them outputs bare relation triplets $(e_h, r, e_t)$ without any indication of \emph{which sentences} in the document support each prediction.
In deployment contexts where predictions feed into clinical knowledge bases, legal due-diligence pipelines, or financial compliance systems, end users cannot verify a prediction without manually locating its textual basis across a multi-page document.

The absence of verifiable evidence creates a practical bottleneck.
Relation extraction outputs are consumed downstream by knowledge graph construction and human decision workflows.

Encoder-based methods have partially addressed this need: \citet{xiao2022sais} introduce sentence-level evidence supervision as an auxiliary signal, and \citet{ma2023dreeam} extend this with dynamic evidence retrieval through memory attention.

The evidence signal \emph{regularizes} the encoder and improves extraction.
In LLM-based DocRE, evidence-grounded extraction requires the model to \emph{generate} complete evidence sentences as part of its output sequence, substantially increasing output length and decoding complexity.
Evidence production in this setting is not an auxiliary signal but an additional generation burden that competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
The fundamental asymmetry is clear: encoder evidence helps extraction; generative evidence costs extraction capacity.
This distinction motivates a systematic investigation of how to produce faithful evidence within LLM-based DocRE without sacrificing the extraction gains that make these models attractive.

We formalize evidence-grounded DocRE as a structured generation task for LLMs and conduct a systematic comparison of three post-training optimization paradigms: online reinforcement learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO; \citealt{shao2024deepseekmath}), offline preference optimization via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO; \citealt{rafailov2023direct}), and offline reinforcement learning via Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT, building on STaR; \citealt{zelikman2022star}).

\section{Conclusion}
\label{sec:conclusion}

This work formalizes evidence-grounded document-level relation extraction as a structured generation task for LLMs and provides the first systematic analysis across 85+ experimental configurations spanning four model scales, two model families, two datasets, and three post-training optimization paradigms.
Our experiments reveal three core findings.
First, RL optimization pressure and evidence-extraction decoupling severity are strongly correlated: GRPO causes catastrophic decoupling, DPO exhibits gradual degradation, and RSFT preserves stable joint performance, a relationship the EDCR diagnostic captures at method-level $\rho = -0.965$.
Second, the cost of joint evidence production follows a non-monotonic, scale-dependent pattern: 1.7B models gain +8pp Ign-F1 from evidence, 4B models pay a $-$7.5pp penalty, and 8B models approach zero cost.
Third, RSFT with NLI-based Contrastive Evidence Discrimination (CED) scoring is the only effective optimization route, yielding +4.92pp Ign-F1 over SFT at 4B scale.
Our 1.7B RSFT model (50.50 Ign-F1) matches 8B SFT performance (50.51), enabling evidence-grounded extraction at a fraction of the computational cost.

Several directions remain open.
Our evaluation relies on exact-match F1, which systematically underestimates generative RE by penalizing valid entity mentions with different surface forms; developing fuzzy matching or embedding-based evaluation protocols would yield more accurate assessment of LLM-based extractors.
Test set evaluation on DocRED via CodaLab submission is pending and will determine whether development-set findings generalize.
The evidence grounding framework extends naturally to other information extraction tasks such as event extraction and slot filling, where output verifiability is equally critical.
Finally, iterative RSFT through multi-round self-taught reasoning may further reduce the evidence tax, particularly at the 4B scale where the penalty is most severe.

3	Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) requires identifying semantic relations between entity pairs across multiple sentences, a task where encoder-based methods such as \citet{zhou2021atlop} long dominated.
4	Recent LLM-based approaches have closed this gap: \citet{wan2024genres} recast DocRE as constrained generation, \citet{xu2024lmrc} frame it as multi-choice reading comprehension, and \citet{chen2025docksrag} combine retrieval-augmented generation with structured knowledge.
5	These methods approach or surpass encoder baselines on DocRED \citep{yao2019docred} and Re-DocRED \citep{tan2022redocred} in extraction accuracy.
6	Yet every one of them outputs bare relation triplets $(e_h, r, e_t)$ without any indication of \emph{which sentences} in the document support each prediction.
7	In deployment contexts where predictions feed into clinical knowledge bases, legal due-diligence pipelines, or financial compliance systems, end users cannot verify a prediction without manually locating its textual basis across a multi-page document.
8	
9	The absence of verifiable evidence creates a practical bottleneck.
10	Relation extraction outputs are consumed downstream by knowledge graph construction and human decision workflows.
11	When a system predicts that a drug interacts with a gene, or that a contract clause implies a liability, practitioners must trace each prediction back to source text before acting on it.
12	Without machine-generated evidence, this verification requires exhaustive manual review of the input document for every predicted relation.
13	Encoder-based methods have partially addressed this need: \citet{xiao2022sais} introduce sentence-level evidence supervision as an auxiliary signal, and \citet{ma2023dreeam} extend this with dynamic evidence retrieval through memory attention.
14	Both improve extraction quality \emph{and} produce evidence annotations.
15	However, encoder methods now trail LLM-based approaches in extraction accuracy, and their evidence mechanisms (binary sentence classification) do not transfer to generative architectures.
16	The community therefore faces a gap: the most accurate extractors provide no evidence, while the evidence-capable methods are no longer competitive.
17	
18	This gap reflects a deeper structural difference between evidence in encoder and generative frameworks.
19	In SAIS and DREEAM, evidence retrieval is a binary classification task (does sentence $s_i$ support relation $r$?) that serves as auxiliary supervision.
20	The evidence signal \emph{regularizes} the encoder and improves extraction.
21	In LLM-based DocRE, evidence-grounded extraction requires the model to \emph{generate} complete evidence sentences as part of its output sequence, substantially increasing output length and decoding complexity.
22	Evidence production in this setting is not an auxiliary signal but an additional generation burden that competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
23	Whether this generation cost necessarily harms extraction, or whether the interaction is more nuanced, remains an open question: the answer may depend on model scale and optimization strategy.
24	This uncertainty motivates a systematic investigation of how evidence production interacts with extraction quality across model scales and optimization paradigms.
25	
26	We formalize evidence-grounded DocRE as a structured generation task for LLMs and conduct a systematic comparison of three post-training optimization paradigms: online reinforcement learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO; \citealt{shao2024deepseekmath}), offline preference optimization via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO; \citealt{rafailov2023direct}), and offline reinforcement learning via Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT, building on STaR; \citealt{zelikman2022star}).
27	Our experiments across 85+ configurations, spanning four model scales (1.7B to 8B), two model families, and two datasets, reveal three principal findings.
28	\textbf{First}, we identify a \emph{decoupling spectrum}: the strength of RL optimization pressure correlates with the severity of evidence-extraction decoupling.
29	GRPO with Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA; \citealt{hu2022lora}) produces catastrophic decoupling where extraction accuracy collapses to near zero; GRPO with full-precision training shows mild decoupling; DPO exhibits gradual degradation; and RSFT maintains stable joint performance.
30	QLoRA acts as a catastrophic amplifier of the underlying optimization conflict rather than its root cause.
31	\textbf{Second}, we discover a \emph{scale-dependent evidence tax}: the cost of jointly producing evidence and relations follows a non-monotonic pattern across model scales.
32	At 1.7B parameters, evidence generation provides an implicit regularization benefit of +8 percentage points (pp) in Ign-F1; at 4B, it imposes a $-$7.5pp penalty; at 8B, the tax approaches zero.
33	This non-linear pattern overturns the naive assumption that evidence generation uniformly harms extraction.
34	\textbf{Third}, RSFT with Natural Language Inference (NLI) based Contrastive Evidence Discrimination (CED) scoring emerges as the only effective optimization route.
35	By selecting high-quality training samples through output filtering rather than applying gradient-based optimization pressure, RSFT sidesteps the multi-objective competition that destabilizes RL and preference methods.

\section{Introduction}

Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) requires identifying semantic relations between entity pairs across multiple sentences, a task where encoder-based methods such as \citet{zhou2021atlop} long dominated.
Recent LLM-based approaches have closed this gap: \citet{wan2024genres} recast DocRE as constrained generation, \citet{xu2024lmrc} frame it as multi-choice reading comprehension, and \citet{chen2025docksrag} combine retrieval-augmented generation with structured knowledge.
These methods approach or surpass encoder baselines on DocRED \citep{yao2019docred} and Re-DocRED \citep{tan2022redocred} in extraction accuracy.
Yet every one of them outputs bare relation triplets $(e_h, r, e_t)$ without any indication of \emph{which sentences} in the document support each prediction.
In deployment contexts where predictions feed into clinical knowledge bases, legal due-diligence pipelines, or financial compliance systems, end users cannot verify a prediction without manually locating its textual basis across a multi-page document.

The absence of verifiable evidence creates a practical bottleneck.
Relation extraction outputs are consumed downstream by knowledge graph construction and human decision workflows.
When a system predicts that a drug interacts with a gene, or that a contract clause implies a liability, practitioners must trace each prediction back to source text before acting on it.
Without machine-generated evidence, this verification requires exhaustive manual review of the input document for every predicted relation.
Encoder-based methods have partially addressed this need: \citet{xiao2022sais} introduce sentence-level evidence supervision as an auxiliary signal, and \citet{ma2023dreeam} extend this with dynamic evidence retrieval through memory attention.
Both improve extraction quality \emph{and} produce evidence annotations.
However, encoder methods now trail LLM-based approaches in extraction accuracy, and their evidence mechanisms (binary sentence classification) do not transfer to generative architectures.
The community therefore faces a gap: the most accurate extractors provide no evidence, while the evidence-capable methods are no longer competitive.

This gap reflects a deeper structural difference between evidence in encoder and generative frameworks.
In SAIS and DREEAM, evidence retrieval is a binary classification task (does sentence $s_i$ support relation $r$?) that serves as auxiliary supervision.
The evidence signal \emph{regularizes} the encoder and improves extraction.
In LLM-based DocRE, evidence-grounded extraction requires the model to \emph{generate} complete evidence sentences as part of its output sequence, substantially increasing output length and decoding complexity.
Evidence production in this setting is not an auxiliary signal but an additional generation burden that competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
Whether this generation cost necessarily harms extraction, or whether the interaction is more nuanced, remains an open question: the answer may depend on model scale and optimization strategy.
This uncertainty motivates a systematic investigation of how evidence production interacts with extraction quality across model scales and optimization paradigms.

We formalize evidence-grounded DocRE as a structured generation task for LLMs and conduct a systematic comparison of three post-training optimization paradigms: online reinforcement learning via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO; \citealt{shao2024deepseekmath}), offline preference optimization via Direct Preference Optimization (DPO; \citealt{rafailov2023direct}), and offline reinforcement learning via Rejection Sampling Fine-Tuning (RSFT, building on STaR; \citealt{zelikman2022star}).
Our experiments across 85+ configurations, spanning four model scales (1.7B to 8B), two model families, and two datasets, reveal three principal findings.
\textbf{First}, we identify a \emph{decoupling spectrum}: the strength of RL optimization pressure correlates with the severity of evidence-extraction decoupling.
GRPO with Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation (QLoRA; \citealt{hu2022lora}) produces catastrophic decoupling where extraction accuracy collapses to near zero; GRPO with full-precision training shows mild decoupling; DPO exhibits gradual degradation; and RSFT maintains stable joint performance.
QLoRA acts as a catastrophic amplifier of the underlying optimization conflict rather than its root cause.
\textbf{Second}, we discover a \emph{scale-dependent evidence tax}: the cost of jointly producing evidence and relations follows a non-monotonic pattern across model scales.
At 1.7B parameters, evidence generation provides an implicit regularization benefit of +8 percentage points (pp) in Ign-F1; at 4B, it imposes a $-$7.5pp penalty; at 8B, the tax approaches zero.
This non-linear pattern overturns the naive assumption that evidence generation uniformly harms extraction.
\textbf{Third}, RSFT with Natural Language Inference (NLI) based Contrastive Evidence Discrimination (CED) scoring emerges as the only effective optimization route.
By selecting high-quality training samples through output filtering rather than applying gradient-based optimization pressure, RSFT sidesteps the multi-objective competition that destabilizes RL and preference methods.

Our contributions are as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item We formalize \textbf{evidence-grounded document-level relation extraction} as a generation task for LLMs, defining structured output formats that jointly produce relation triplets and their supporting evidence sentences.

    \item We characterize a \textbf{decoupling spectrum} across optimization paradigms: RL optimization pressure correlates with evidence-extraction decoupling severity (GRPO catastrophic $\rightarrow$ DPO gradual $\rightarrow$ RSFT none). We introduce the Evidence-Decoupling Ratio (EDCR), a diagnostic that quantifies the degree of misalignment between extraction and evidence capabilities, capturing this relationship with method-level $\rho = -0.965$.

    \item We identify a \textbf{scale-dependent evidence tax}: a non-monotonic cost pattern across 1.7B, 4B, and 8B parameters that overturns the assumption that evidence production uniformly degrades extraction quality.

    \item We establish \textbf{RSFT with NLI-based CED scoring} as an effective solution, achieving +5.38pp Ign-F1 over SFT at 4B scale (best seed). Our 1.7B RSFT model (50.50 Ign-F1) matches 8B SFT performance (50.51), enabling deployment-efficient evidence-grounded extraction at reduced computational cost.

    \item We present a \textbf{comprehensive empirical study} spanning 85+ experiments across four model scales, two model families, two datasets (DocRED, Re-DocRED), and three optimization paradigms, providing the first systematic analysis of evidence production in generative DocRE.
\end{enumerate}

papers:

  # === Category 1: Reward Diversity / Reward Shaping for RL Stability ===

  - title: "GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL Optimization"
    authors: NVIDIA Labs
    year: 2025
    venue: ICML 2026
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05242
    category: reward_diversity
    role: closest_prior_work
    key_finding: >
      直接将 GRPO 应用于多 reward 组合时，不同 rollout 的 reward 组合在归一化后 collapse 为相同 advantage 值，
      降低训练信号分辨率导致收敛失败。GDPO 对每个 reward 独立做 group-wise normalization 再聚合，
      保留多 reward 的相对差异，显著提升训练稳定性。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      最直接相关。CED reward 本质上引入了独立于 extraction F1 的 reward 维度（evidence quality），
      GDPO 的理论分析解释了为什么多维 reward 比单一 reward 更稳定——独立 reward 维度防止 advantage collapse。
      但 GDPO 是方法论贡献，CED 是 task-specific reward 设计自然具备了这一特性。

  - title: "DRA-GRPO: Exploring Diversity-Aware Reward Adjustment for R1-Zero-Like Training of LLMs"
    authors: Xiwen Chen et al.
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2505.09655
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09655
    category: reward_diversity
    role: related_method
    key_finding: >
      GRPO 的标量 reward 无法区分语义多样但得分相同的输出（diversity-quality inconsistency）。
      DRA 用子模互信息（SMI）对 reward 加权，给多样性高的 completion 更大权重，
      等价于 Inverse Propensity Scoring 去偏，防止 policy 坍缩到先验模式。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      DRA 通过后处理 reward 注入多样性信号；CED 的 reward 本身就内含对比结构自然提供 diversity 信号。
      机制互补但来源不同——CED 是 reward design 层面，DRA 是 optimization 层面。

  - title: "Shrinking the Variance: Shrinkage Baselines for RL with Verifiable Rewards"
    authors: Guanning Zeng et al.
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2511.03710
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.03710
    category: reward_diversity
    role: theoretical_support
    key_finding: >
      RLVR 中 per-prompt 均值 baseline 在低 generation 数下估计不准导致高 variance 梯度。
      用 James-Stein shrinkage 混合 per-prompt 和 cross-prompt 均值，
      构造可证明更低 variance 的 policy gradient estimator。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      理论支持：reward variance 对 gradient estimation 质量至关重要。
      CED 的额外 reward 维度提供更丰富的 per-group variance，间接起到 variance 维持效果。

  - title: "Reward Shaping to Mitigate Reward Hacking in RLHF"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2502.18770
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.18770
    category: reward_diversity
    role: background
    key_finding: >
      RL reward 应有界且先快速增长后缓慢收敛。系统研究 reward shaping 原则，
      好的 reward 形状能抑制 reward hacking 并提升训练稳定性。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      CED reward 的 0-1 对比判别结构天然满足有界性，
      且 evidence quality 的渐进提升符合"先快后慢"的 reward shaping 原则。

  # === Category 2: Mode Collapse Prevention in GRPO/RLHF ===

  - title: "DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale"
    authors: ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua AIR
    year: 2025
    venue: NeurIPS 2025
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14476
    category: mode_collapse_prevention
    role: key_baseline
    key_finding: >
      Naive GRPO 存在 entropy collapse（policy 熵快速下降→输出同质化）。
      根因：clipping 不对称性——概率 0.01 的 token 最多增到 0.012，而概率 0.9 的 token 可达 1.08，
      低概率 token 难以增长，抑制探索。DAPO 提出 Clip-Higher（εhigh=0.28 > εlow=0.2）
      为低概率 token 留更大增长空间，加 Dynamic Sampling 过滤 accuracy=0 或 1 的 prompt
      （这些 prompt 产生零梯度，降低有效 batch size）。在 AIME 2024 达 50 分超越 DeepSeek-R1-Zero。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      DAPO 从 optimization 技巧角度解决 entropy collapse。CED reward 从 reward design 层面
      防止 mode collapse——evidence quality 维度确保 reward 组内有足够 variance，
      不会出现 all-same-reward 的零梯度 prompt。DAPO 的 Dynamic Sampling 过滤 accuracy=0/1 prompt
      与我们观察到的 frac_zero_std→0.8 现象本质相同：extraction-only reward 下大量 prompt
      产生零 advantage，CED 从源头（reward 设计）而非后处理（过滤）解决这个问题。

  - title: "Dr. GRPO: Removing Optimization Bias in GRPO"
    authors: Liu et al.
    year: 2025
    venue: COLM 2025
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783
    category: mode_collapse_prevention
    role: related_analysis
    key_finding: >
      GRPO 的 std 归一化引入两个 bias：(1) difficulty bias——std(r) 归一化对低 variance 组
      （全对/全错）给予过高 advantage 权重，trivial question 主导训练信号；
      (2) length bias——per-token loss 的 1/|o_i| 项使长的错误回答被 under-penalize。
      当 std(r)→0 时 advantage 爆炸或未定义，梯度数值不稳定。
      Dr. GRPO 移除 std 归一化，用无偏 Monte Carlo advantage：Ã = R(q,o_i) - mean(R)。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      与我们的实验发现高度一致：extraction-only reward 下 frac_zero_std→0.8 正是
      Dr. GRPO 分析的 difficulty bias 极端情况——大量 prompt 的所有 rollout 得到相同 F1，
      std→0 导致 advantage 异常。CED 通过增加 reward 维度天然维持 reward_std>0，
      从 reward 设计而非算法修改角度避免了 Dr. GRPO 发现的 bias。

  - title: "GVPO: Group Variance Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2025
    venue: NeurIPS 2025
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19599
    category: mode_collapse_prevention
    role: alternative_framework
    key_finding: >
      将 KL 约束 reward 最大化的解析解直接嵌入梯度权重，
      variance 项自然平衡 exploration 与 exploitation，维持适度 entropy。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      GVPO 的 variance 项机制与 CED 维持 reward variance 的效果功能类似，
      但 GVPO 是算法层面 implicit regularization，CED 是 reward 层面 explicit structure。

  - title: "REINFORCE++: Stabilizing Critic-Free Policy Optimization with Global Advantage Normalization"
    authors: Jian Hu et al.
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2501.03262
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.03262
    category: mode_collapse_prevention
    role: related_method
    key_finding: >
      Prompt-level (local) advantage normalization 导致不准确估计和过拟合。
      Global batch normalization 提供更稳定、理论无偏的 gradient estimator。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      解决 local normalization 的 variance 问题；CED 从 reward 端增加 variance 来源。
      两者在不同层面解决同一问题：防止 gradient signal 消失。

  - title: "DiverseGRPO: Mitigating Mode Collapse in Image Generation via Diversity-Aware GRPO"
    authors: Henglin Liu et al.
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2512.21514
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.21514
    category: mode_collapse_prevention
    role: parallel_work
    key_finding: >
      图像生成中 GRPO 后期输出同质化。distributional reward modeling（谱聚类+exploratory reward）
      和 structure-aware regularization 实现 13-18% 语义多样性提升。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      跨域验证了 GRPO mode collapse 的普遍性，distributional reward 思路与 CED 精神相近——
      都是通过 reward 层面结构化信号维持输出多样性。

  - title: "Why GRPO Needs Normalization: A Local-Curvature Perspective on Adaptive Gradients"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2601.23135
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.23135
    category: mode_collapse_prevention
    role: theoretical_support
    key_finding: >
      GRPO 的 reward_std 归一化在温和条件下提供严格优于未归一化 REINFORCE 的收敛速率，
      收益由 prompt 间平均 reward std 刻画。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      直接理论支撑：reward_std 越大收敛越好。CED 通过 evidence quality 维度维持高 reward_std，
      从该理论看 CED 的稳定性优势是 reward_std 维持带来的收敛速率优势。

  # === Category 3: Contrastive Rewards in RL ===

  - title: "Improving Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback Using Contrastive Rewards"
    authors: Shen, Zhang et al.
    year: 2024
    venue: arXiv 2403.07708
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07708
    category: contrastive_reward
    role: closest_contrastive_precedent
    key_finding: >
      两步机制：(1) 离线采样 baseline response；(2) 用 baseline 计算 contrastive reward
      作为 PPO 的 penalty 项。效果：惩罚 reward uncertainty、根据任务难度自适应校准、
      减少 PPO 中的 variance。在 TL;DR 和 HH-RLHF 上持续优于标准 RLHF。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      最接近的对比 reward 先例。关键差异：(1) 它是对 learned RM 输出的后处理对比，
      CED 是 reward function 本身就是对比判别（evidence vs. corrupted evidence）；
      (2) 它在 PPO 中验证，CED 在 GRPO 中验证；
      (3) 它是 domain-agnostic penalty，CED 是 task-specific faithfulness signal。
      stabilizing 机制相通但实现路径根本不同。

  - title: "Improving Discriminative Capability of Reward Models in RLHF Using Contrastive Learning"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2024
    venue: EMNLP 2024
    url: https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.852/
    category: contrastive_reward
    role: related_method
    key_finding: >
      无监督对比损失训练 reward model 充分捕捉对比数据区分度，
      带来更稳定的 PPO 训练 return 和 reward。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      验证对比训练 reward model → 更稳定 RL 训练链条。CED 不是对比训练 reward model，
      而是 reward function 本身就是对比判别，但 stabilizing 机制相通。

  - title: "Contrastive Preference Learning: Learning from Human Feedback without RL"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2024
    venue: ICLR 2025
    url: https://openreview.net/forum?id=iX1RjVQODj
    category: contrastive_reward
    role: background
    key_finding: >
      将 preference learning 重新表述为对比学习问题，无需显式 RL 即可从人类反馈中学习。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      对比框架在 preference alignment 中的通用性。CED 可被视为 task-specific contrastive preference signal。

  # === Category 4: Evidence-Based Rewards in IE/NLP ===

  - title: "Drift: Enhancing LLM Faithfulness in Rationale Generation"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2025
    venue: ACL 2025
    url: https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.340.pdf
    category: evidence_reward
    role: related_method
    key_finding: >
      用 faithfulness reward 引导 LLM 生成更可靠的 rationale，提升 CoT 推理事实一致性。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      Faithfulness reward 用于生成质量的先例。CED 中 evidence discrimination
      本质上也是 faithfulness 信号——判断证据是否忠实支持抽取结果。

  - title: "Fine-Grained NLI-Based Faithfulness Evaluation for Diverse Summarisation Tasks (INFUSE)"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2024
    venue: EACL 2024
    url: https://aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-long.102/
    category: evidence_reward
    role: background
    key_finding: >
      变长前提+简化假设的细粒度 NLI faithfulness 评估，超越传统 NLI 在多任务摘要上的表现。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      NLI 作为 faithfulness 评估工具的进展。CED 中 NLI 组件用于判断 evidence 对 triple 的支持度。

  - title: "Enhancing Cross-Evidence Reasoning Graph for Document-Level Relation Extraction"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2024
    venue: PMC/Bioinformatics 2024
    url: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232587/
    category: evidence_reward
    role: background
    key_finding: >
      文档级关系抽取中用 cross-evidence reasoning graph 增强跨证据推理。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      DocRE 中 evidence 的重要性。但用 evidence 作为模型输入特征，
      我们用 evidence quality 作为 RL reward 信号——定位根本不同。

  # === Category 5: Multi-Objective RL for Text Generation ===

  - title: "Confronting Reward Model Overoptimization with Constrained RLHF"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2025
    venue: OpenReview
    url: https://openreview.net/forum?id=gkfUvn0fLU
    category: multi_objective_rl
    role: related_analysis
    key_finding: >
      多组件 RM 的 overoptimization 研究。component RM 间的相关性显著影响 overoptimization 临界点，
      用 constrained MDP 防止超出适当边界。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      CED 引入了与 extraction F1 低相关的 reward component（evidence quality），
      根据该论文分析低相关多组件 reward 更不易 overoptimize，
      可能是 CED 稳定性的另一个理论解释角度。

  - title: "On-Policy RL with Optimal Reward Baseline"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2505.23585
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.23585
    category: multi_objective_rl
    role: theoretical_support
    key_finding: >
      Optimal baseline 一致性地实现更高训练 reward 和更高 entropy，
      有效稳定训练并促进更多样的 policy exploration。
    relevance_to_ced_stabilizer: >
      CED reward 的多维特性可能起到类似 optimal baseline 效果——
      evidence quality 维度为 advantage estimation 提供更丰富的参照信号。

  # === Category 6: RSFT Methodology & Theory ===

  - title: "A Minimalist Approach to LLM Reasoning: from Rejection Sampling to Reinforce"
    authors: Xiao et al.
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2504.11343
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.11343
    category: rsft_methodology
    role: key_theoretical_support
    key_finding: >
      RAFT（简单 rejection sampling baseline）在数学推理上与 GRPO/PPO 表现相当。
      消融实验表明 GRPO 的主要优势来自丢弃全错 prompt 而非 reward normalization。
      提出 Reinforce-Rej，在 RAFT 基础上过滤全对和全错 sample。
      关键洞察：GRPO 和 RAFT 的核心区别在于负样本处理——GRPO 混合正负样本训练，
      RAFT 只用正样本，但 RAFT 仍能达到相当性能，说明 rejection sampling 的简单性被低估了。
    relevance_to_rsft_docre: >
      直接支持我们的设计选择：(1) RSFT 在 DocRE 上成功而 GRPO 失败，
      与该论文发现一致——rejection sampling 的 offline 特性天然避免了 catastrophic forgetting；
      (2) GRPO 主要优势来自过滤全错 prompt，这与我们 RSFT 的 reward-based filtering 机制相同；
      (3) DocRE structured output 比 math reasoning 更难用 online RL 优化，
      强化了 offline RSFT 的合理性。

  - title: "Beyond Rejection Sampling: Trajectory Fusion for Scaling Mathematical Reasoning (TrajFusion)"
    authors: Jie Deng et al.
    year: 2026
    venue: arXiv 2602.04391
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04391
    category: rsft_methodology
    role: method_component
    key_finding: >
      传统 RSFT 只用正确轨迹，丢弃错误轨迹。TrajFusion 将错误和正确轨迹交替拼接，
      显式建模试错推理过程，在困难数学问题上显著超越标准 RFT。
    relevance_to_rsft_docre: >
      Future work 方向：可考虑在 DocRE RSFT 中融合失败样本的信息。
      但 DocRE 的结构化输出（JSON triple）不同于 math 的 chain-of-thought，
      融合方式需要重新设计。

  - title: "Rejection Sampling Based Fine Tuning Secretly Performs PPO"
    authors: Anonymous
    year: 2025
    venue: ICML 2025
    url: https://openreview.net/forum?id=yQ2UivKlir
    category: rsft_methodology
    role: theoretical_support
    key_finding: >
      建立 RSFT 与 PPO 之间的理论联系：rejection sampling fine-tuning
      在特定条件下隐式执行 PPO with marginal KL constraints。
    relevance_to_rsft_docre: >
      为 RSFT 的有效性提供理论解释。我们的 RSFT 成功可被视为
      隐式执行了 constrained policy optimization，
      避免了显式 GRPO 在 structured output 上的不稳定性。

  # === Category 7: RL for Information Extraction ===

  - title: "R1-RE: Cross-Domain Relation Extraction with RLVR"
    authors: Runpeng Dai, Tong Zheng et al.
    year: 2025
    venue: arXiv 2507.04642
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04642
    category: rl_for_ie
    role: direct_competitor
    key_finding: >
      首个将 RLVR（GRPO + verifiable reward）用于关系抽取的框架。
      将 RE 重构为推理任务，R1-RE-7B 在跨域 OOD 准确率约 70%，媲美 GPT-4o。
      Reward 设计：format reward (+1/-3) + metric reward (+2/-1.5)，先验证格式再加准确度。
      triplet extraction 用 F1-based reward（entity weight=1, triplet weight=3）。
      未报告 catastrophic forgetting——GRPO 训练后在 MATH-500/IFEval/GPQA 上性能不降反升，
      说明句子级 RE 的简单 reward 结构足以稳定 GRPO 训练。
    results:
      sem2010_in_domain: 91.8
      sem2010_ood: 66.5
      mdkg_in_domain: 88.1
      mdkg_ood: 65.8
    evidence_generation: false
    relevance_to_rsft_docre: >
      最直接竞争者。关键差异与讨论：
      (1) R1-RE 是句子级 RE，GRPO 成功；我们是文档级 RE，GRPO 失败→RSFT 成功。

      (3) R1-RE 关注 OOD 泛化，无 evidence 组件；我们关注 evidence-grounded extraction quality。
      互补而非直接冲突——R1-RE 证明 RLVR for RE 可行，我们揭示文档级需要额外设计。

  # === Category 13: Evidence-Grounded RL (NEW - 2026-05-15 scan) ===

  - title: "EvidenceRL: Reinforcing Evidence Consistency for Trustworthy Language Models"
    authors: Ben Tamo, Lu, Marteau, Nnamdi, Wang
    year: 2026
    venue: arXiv 2603.19532
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19532
    category: evidence_grounded_rl
    role: closest_competitor
    key_finding: >
      用 GRPO 同时优化 grounding（evidence entailment）和 correctness（答案准确性）。
      在 cardiac diagnosis（Llama-3.2-3B）上 F1@3 从 37.0→54.5，grounding 从 47.6→78.2，
      hallucination 降 5 倍。在 legal reasoning（Llama-3.1-8B）上 faithfulness 从 32.8%→67.6%。
      核心：证据一致性 reward 不牺牲 task accuracy 的前提下大幅提升 faithfulness。
    relevance_to_freige: >
      **最直接的 novelty 威胁。** EvidenceRL 与 FREIGE 共享核心 idea：用 GRPO + evidence faithfulness reward
      训练更可靠的模型。关键差异：(1) EvidenceRL 在 QA 域（cardiac/legal），不涉及 DocRE 的 structured output；
      (2) EvidenceRL 未报告 evidence generation 的 performance cost（evidence tax）——它的 grounding 和
      correctness 同时提升，而我们发现 DocRE 中两者存在 ~8pp 张力；
      (3) EvidenceRL 不涉及 task decoupling 现象（QLoRA-specific）；
      (4) EvidenceRL 无 inference-time reranking（CED reranker）。
      定位策略：EvidenceRL 证明 evidence-grounded RL 在 QA 域有效，
      我们揭示 DocRE structured output 带来的独特挑战（evidence tax、task decoupling）和解法（CED reranker）。

      解释了为什么单一 extraction F1 reward 下模型可能 hack 到 "忽略 evidence 只抽 triple" 的策略。
      CED 从 reward 设计端解决，MO-GRPO 从算法端解决，互补视角。

      FlyLoRA 的解决方案（分配不同 rank 给不同任务）验证了 rank capacity 是 decoupling 的关键因素。

      最直接的 prior work——同时做 RE 和 evidence prediction 的代表方法。
      关键区别：SAIS 是 encoder-based discriminative model 用 attention supervision，
      FREIGE 是 generative LLM 用 text-level evidence generation。
      SAIS 发现 evidence supervision 提升 RE，而 FREIGE 发现 generative evidence 有 ~8pp cost，
      这个差异正是 FREIGE 论文的核心发现之一。

  # === Category 39: Knowledge Distillation for DocRE ===

  - title: "Document-Level Relation Extraction with Adaptive Focal Loss and Knowledge Distillation"
    authors: Qingyu Tan, Ruidan He, Lidong Bing, Hwee Tou Ng
    year: 2022
    venue: Findings of ACL 2022
    url: https://aclanthology.org/2022.findings-acl.132/
    category: knowledge_distillation_docre
    role: background
    key_finding: >
      KD-DocRE：用 axial attention 学习 entity pair 间依赖关系，
      adaptive focal loss 解决类别不均衡，knowledge distillation 弥合
      人工标注和远程监督数据的差异。DocRED leaderboard 上超越前 SOTA 1.36 F1。
    relevance_to_freige: >
      KD 方法在 DocRE 中有效，暗示了 FREIGE 的 RSFT（rejection sampling fine-tuning）
      本质上也是一种 self-distillation——用模型自身的高质量输出训练自身。
      但 KD-DocRE 是 encoder-based discriminative，FREIGE 是 generative paradigm。

  - title: "Document-level Relation Extraction with Progressive Self-distillation"
    authors: Zhenlan Zhai, Shang Gao, Leilei Gan, Shan Zhao
    year: 2024
    venue: ACM TOIS 2024
    url: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3656168
    category: knowledge_distillation_docre
    role: related_method
    key_finding: >
      PSD：online self-knowledge distillation 用过去预测作为 soft labels，
      无需额外 teacher model，单次训练即可完成。
      渐进式 soft label 平滑 hard label 的噪声，提升 DocRE 性能。
    relevance_to_freige: >
      Self-distillation 思路与 FREIGE 的 RSFT 有共通之处——
      都是利用模型自身能力产生训练信号。但 PSD 是 discriminative 模型的 label smoothing，
      RSFT 是 generative 模型的 output selection，机制不同。

  # === Category 40: Evaluation for Generative RE ===

  - title: "GenRES: Rethinking Evaluation for Generative Relation Extraction in the Era of Large Language Models"
    authors: Pengcheng Jiang, Jiacheng Lin, Zifeng Wang, Jimeng Sun, Jiawei Han
    year: 2024
    venue: NAACL 2024
    url: https://aclanthology.org/2024.naacl-long.155/
    category: evaluation_generative_re
    role: evaluation_method
    key_finding: >
      传统 precision/recall 基于 exact match 无法公平评估 generative RE——
      LLM 输出的关系在语义上正确但与参考标注不完全匹配。
      提出 multi-dimensional 评估框架：topic similarity, uniqueness, granularity,
      factualness, completeness。发现 human-annotated relations 自身也有不完整性。
    relevance_to_freige: >
      FREIGE 使用 generative RE format，GenRES 的发现验证了
      exact match F1 可能低估 generative RE 性能。论文中需讨论此 evaluation limitation。
      但 FREIGE 的 re-DocRED evaluation 已有较完善的标签，影响可能较小。

  # === Category 41: Self-Training / Bootstrapping for LLM Reasoning ===

  - title: "STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning"
    authors: Eric Zelikman, Yuhuai Wu, Jesse Mu, Noah D. Goodman
    year: 2022
    venue: NeurIPS 2022
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.14465
    category: self_training_bootstrapping
    role: method_component
    key_finding: >
      Self-Taught Reasoner：迭代式 bootstrapping——生成 rationale 回答问题，
      答对的保留，答错的用 rationalization（给正确答案生成事后 rationale）补充，
      然后 fine-tune 模型。循环迭代使模型逐渐学会更难的推理。
    relevance_to_freige: >
      STaR 的 iterative bootstrapping 是 FREIGE RSFT 的理论先驱——
      RSFT 本质上是 STaR 的一个 iteration（生成、筛选正确输出、fine-tune）。
      但 FREIGE 加入了 evidence quality 作为额外筛选维度，
      不只看 answer correctness 还看 evidence faithfulness。

  - title: "Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models"
    authors: Zixiang Chen, Yihe Deng, Huizhuo Yuan, Kaixuan Ji, Quanquan Gu
    year: 2024
    venue: ICML 2024
    url: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01335
    category: self_training_bootstrapping
    role: related_method
    key_finding: >
      SPIN：LLM 通过 self-play 机制与自身过去版本对弈来提升——
      区分自身生成的 response 和 human-annotated response。
      全局最优在 LLM policy 与目标分布对齐时达到。
      性能超越 DPO + GPT-4 偏好数据。
    relevance_to_freige: >
      SPIN 的 self-play 和 FREIGE 的 RSFT 都是利用模型自身输出进行训练的方法，
      但方向不同：SPIN 学习区分 self vs human，RSFT 选择 self 中的最优。
      理论上 SPIN 可应用于 DocRE 的 evidence 生成质量提升。

## Paper Overview

R1-RE addresses relation extraction (RE), a core task in natural language processing, by reframing it as a reasoning task guided by annotation guidelines and introducing the first reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR) framework for RE tasks.

## Main Contributions

The method elicits the reasoning abilities of small language models for annotation tasks, resulting in significantly improved out-of-domain (OOD) robustness. The framework is inspired by the recent success of reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR), which has proven effective in promoting reasoning skills in smaller models on challenging domains such as mathematics and code generation.

## Performance Results

The R1-RE-7B model attains an average out-of-domain accuracy of approximately 70%, on par with leading proprietary models such as GPT-4o.

## Datasets and Evaluation

The approach is evaluated on the public SemEval-2010 dataset and a private MDKG dataset.

## Authors

The paper is by Runpeng Dai and colleagues, with the arXiv identifier 2507.04642, published in July 2025.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about E-GRPO related to NER (Named Entity Recognition) and entity-aware reward optimization:

## E-GRPO: Entity-aware Group Relative Policy Optimization

Entity-aware Group Relative Policy Optimization (E-GRPO) is a reinforcement learning (RL) framework developed to fine-tune LLM search agents using dense entity-aware rewards. It actively repurposes synthetic entity annotations embedded in question-answering (QA) tasks and complex research queries, leveraging ground-truth entity information for effective supervision.

### Key Contributions

E-GRPO systematically addresses key limitations of standard Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) by providing granular feedback on the reasoning traces of LLM agents, thereby enhancing sample efficiency, reasoning quality, and overall alignment in knowledge-intensive environments (Zhao et al., 28 Oct 2025).

### Reward Design

It formulates rewards based on normalized entity match rates, crediting near-miss reasoning with partial credit and enhancing sample efficiency. E-GRPO diverges from traditional approaches by proposing a reward signal that is both fine-grained and computationally efficient, requiring no additional annotation, model training, or complex sampling, leveraging ground-truth entities discarded during synthetic data generation as a powerful proxy for factual correctness.

### Empirical Results

Empirical evaluations show E-GRPO significantly improves Pass@1 and Pass@3 metrics across QA and research tasks compared to standard GRPO.

The paper (arXiv:2510.24694) appears to be from October 2025 and addresses a significant limitation of standard GRPO by utilizing entity annotations that are typically embedded in synthetic QA datasets.

## Paper Overview

The paper "RL Is Neither a Panacea Nor a Mirage: Understanding Supervised vs. Reinforcement Learning Fine-Tuning for LLMs" addresses how post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement-learning fine-tuning (RL-FT, e.g., PPO) reshape model representation and out-of-distribution performance.

## Key Findings

The research presents three main findings:

1. **RL can partially recover OOD losses**: RL-FT can restore much of the OOD performance loss from SFT (e.g., Llama-11B 8.97% to 15.38%, Qwen-7B 17.09% to 19.66%), but when SFT induces severe overfitting and a clear distribution shift, RL-FT cannot fully recover OOD performance.

2. **Direction matters more than magnitude**: Direction shifts of singular vectors matter more than singular value magnitudes, with these shifts concentrating on directions linked to the largest and smallest singular values, leaving the bulk spectrum intact.

3. **RL serves as memory restoration**: In two-stage post-training, RL primarily serves as memory restoration rather than creation capability of OOD generalization.

## Methodology

The study uses an out-of-distribution (OOD) variant of the 24-point card game and new spectrum-based diagnostics to analyze how these two stages reshape model representation and OOD performance.

**Paper Details**: arXiv:2508.16546, submitted August 22, 2025, by Hangzhan Jin and colleagues.

1	\section{Related Work}
2	\label{sec:related_work}
3	
4	Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) requires reasoning across sentence boundaries to identify relations between entity pairs.
5	DocRED \citep{yao2019docred} established the first large-scale benchmark for this task, catalyzing a line of encoder-based methods that treat DocRE as classification over entity pair representations.
6	ATLOP \citep{zhou2021atlop} introduced adaptive thresholding for multi-label prediction, and KD-DocRE \citep{tan2022kddocre} applied knowledge distillation to bridge the teacher-student performance gap.
7	A parallel thread incorporates sentence-level evidence into these architectures.
8	SAIS \citep{xiao2022sais} introduced evidence supervision as an auxiliary training signal and showed that joint evidence prediction improves extraction through data augmentation and ensemble inference.
9	DREEAM \citep{ma2023dreeam} extended this approach with dynamic memory-based evidence retrieval that guides attention to supporting sentences.
10	EIDER \citep{xie2022eider} jointly trains an evidence extractor and fuses evidence representations into the relation classifier.
11	In all three systems, evidence identification is binary sentence classification over a fixed candidate set, a formulation that adds no output complexity.
12	Recent work has recast DocRE for large language models.
13	\citet{wan2024genres} reformulate extraction as constrained generation with entity-aware decoding.
14	\citet{xu2024lmrc} frame it as multi-choice reading comprehension, which restricts outputs to predefined options and reduces the generation burden.
15	\citet{chen2025docksrag} combine retrieval-augmented generation with structured knowledge to ground predictions in document context.
16	AutoRE \citep{autore2024} introduces a relation-head-facts decomposition that fine-tunes LLMs with QLoRA for end-to-end DocRE.
17	These methods match or surpass encoder baselines in extraction accuracy but produce bare triplets without evidence.
18	The critical distinction between encoder and generative evidence lies in their computational nature.
19	In SAIS and DREEAM, evidence retrieval is a classification task that regularizes the encoder and improves extraction without increasing output length.
20	In LLM-based DocRE, evidence production requires additional output tokens for each predicted triple, and this generation burden competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
21	This asymmetry explains why evidence ``helps'' in encoder methods but can ``hurt'' in generative ones: the two paradigms operate on fundamentally different forms of evidence integration.
22	
23	Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), introduced by \citet{shao2024deepseekmath}, computes advantages within groups of sampled outputs to eliminate the need for a separate value network.
24	Recent applications have extended GRPO to structured information extraction: E-GRPO \citep{zhao2025egrpo} incorporates entity-aware rewards for named entity recognition, and R1-RE \citep{dai2025r1re} applies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to relation extraction.
25	Direct Preference Optimization \citep{rafailov2023direct} reformulates RLHF as implicit reward maximization through preference pairs, without explicit reward models.
26	Recent analyses argue that RL fine-tuning does not cause catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge \citep{jin2025rl_panacea}.
27	Our findings are compatible with this conclusion but address a distinct phenomenon.
28	The decoupling we observe is an intra-task multi-objective trade-off where extraction and evidence generation compete for model capacity within a single task, rather than knowledge loss across separate tasks.
29	The mild decoupling under bf16 GRPO confirms this interpretation: the model retains its extraction capability but shifts resource allocation under evidence reward pressure.
30	Reward overoptimization, where proxy reward scores increase while true performance degrades, is a known risk in RLHF \citep{gao2023scaling}.
31	Constrained RLHF has been proposed to mitigate this effect in multi-objective settings \citep{moskovitz2024constrained}.
32	Our decoupling spectrum represents a new instance of intra-task reward overoptimization, where evidence rewards crowd out extraction quality.
33	QLoRA compounds this problem: the quantized parameter space constrains effective capacity, and the divergence between quantized and full-precision actors grows over extended training, which amplifies the underlying multi-objective conflict.
34	
35	\citet{zelikman2022star} introduced STaR, an iterative self-improvement method that trains language models on their own correct outputs and bootstraps with rationale augmentation for initially incorrect problems.
36	Subsequent work has extended this framework to mathematical reasoning, code generation, and instruction following.
37	Our RSFT procedure is a single-round variant: the model samples multiple candidate outputs per input, a quality filter selects the best response, and the model trains on the filtered set without iteration.
38	The contribution of RSFT in our setting is not the self-training framework, which is well-established, but its application to evidence-grounded DocRE with CED/NLI scoring as a domain-specific quality filter.
39	This application reveals a structural advantage of discrete output selection over gradient-based optimization for multi-output tasks.
40	Because RSFT selects complete outputs rather than differentiating through a reward signal, it cannot exploit the extraction-evidence trade-off that GRPO and DPO discover through gradient updates.
41	The filtering mechanism inherently preserves joint quality: it retains outputs that are simultaneously good at extraction and evidence production, rather than allowing one objective to dominate the other.
42

\section{Related Work}
\label{sec:related_work}

Document-level relation extraction (DocRE) requires reasoning across sentence boundaries to identify relations between entity pairs.
DocRED \citep{yao2019docred} established the first large-scale benchmark for this task, catalyzing a line of encoder-based methods that treat DocRE as classification over entity pair representations.
ATLOP \citep{zhou2021atlop} introduced adaptive thresholding for multi-label prediction, and KD-DocRE \citep{tan2022kddocre} applied knowledge distillation to bridge the teacher-student performance gap.
A parallel thread incorporates sentence-level evidence into these architectures.
SAIS \citep{xiao2022sais} introduced evidence supervision as an auxiliary training signal and showed that joint evidence prediction improves extraction through data augmentation and ensemble inference.
DREEAM \citep{ma2023dreeam} extended this approach with dynamic memory-based evidence retrieval that guides attention to supporting sentences.
EIDER \citep{xie2022eider} jointly trains an evidence extractor and fuses evidence representations into the relation classifier.
In all three systems, evidence identification is binary sentence classification over a fixed candidate set, a formulation that adds no output complexity.
Recent work has recast DocRE for large language models.
\citet{wan2024genres} reformulate extraction as constrained generation with entity-aware decoding.
\citet{xu2024lmrc} frame it as multi-choice reading comprehension, which restricts outputs to predefined options and reduces the generation burden.
\citet{chen2025docksrag} combine retrieval-augmented generation with structured knowledge to ground predictions in document context.
AutoRE \citep{autore2024} introduces a relation-head-facts decomposition that fine-tunes LLMs with QLoRA for end-to-end DocRE.
These methods match or surpass encoder baselines in extraction accuracy but produce bare triplets without evidence.
The critical distinction between encoder and generative evidence lies in their computational nature.
In SAIS and DREEAM, evidence retrieval is a classification task that regularizes the encoder and improves extraction without increasing output length.
In LLM-based DocRE, evidence production requires additional output tokens for each predicted triple, and this generation burden competes with the extraction objective for model capacity.
This asymmetry explains why evidence ``helps'' in encoder methods but can ``hurt'' in generative ones: the two paradigms operate on fundamentally different forms of evidence integration.

Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), introduced by \citet{shao2024deepseekmath}, computes advantages within groups of sampled outputs to eliminate the need for a separate value network.
Recent applications have extended GRPO to structured information extraction: E-GRPO \citep{zhao2025egrpo} incorporates entity-aware rewards for named entity recognition, and R1-RE \citep{dai2025r1re} applies reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to relation extraction.
Direct Preference Optimization \citep{rafailov2023direct} reformulates RLHF as implicit reward maximization through preference pairs, without explicit reward models.
Recent analyses argue that RL fine-tuning does not cause catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained knowledge \citep{jin2025rl_panacea}.
Our findings are compatible with this conclusion but address a distinct phenomenon.
The decoupling we observe is an intra-task multi-objective trade-off where extraction and evidence generation compete for model capacity within a single task, rather than knowledge loss across separate tasks.
The mild decoupling under bf16 GRPO confirms this interpretation: the model retains its extraction capability but shifts resource allocation under evidence reward pressure.
Reward overoptimization, where proxy reward scores increase while true performance degrades, is a known risk in RLHF \citep{gao2023scaling}.
Constrained RLHF has been proposed to mitigate this effect in multi-objective settings \citep{moskovitz2024constrained}.
Our decoupling spectrum represents a new instance of intra-task reward overoptimization, where evidence rewards crowd out extraction quality.
QLoRA compounds this problem: the quantized parameter space constrains effective capacity, and the divergence between quantized and full-precision actors grows over extended training, which amplifies the underlying multi-objective conflict.

\citet{zelikman2022star} introduced STaR, an iterative self-improvement method that trains language models on their own correct outputs and bootstraps with rationale augmentation for initially incorrect problems.
Subsequent work has extended this framework to mathematical reasoning, code generation, and instruction following.
Our RSFT procedure is a single-round variant: the model samples multiple candidate outputs per input, a quality filter selects the best response, and the model trains on the filtered set without iteration.
The contribution of RSFT in our setting is not the self-training framework, which is well-established, but its application to evidence-grounded DocRE with CED/NLI scoring as a domain-specific quality filter.
This application reveals a structural advantage of discrete output selection over gradient-based optimization for multi-output tasks.
Because RSFT selects complete outputs rather than differentiating through a reward signal, it cannot exploit the extraction-evidence trade-off that GRPO and DPO discover through gradient updates.
The filtering mechanism inherently preserves joint quality: it retains outputs that are simultaneously good at extraction and evidence production, rather than allowing one objective to dominate the other.

I found comprehensive information about GDPO on arXiv. Here's what the research reveals:

## Overview

GDPO (Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization) is presented in arXiv paper 2601.05242, authored by Shih-Yang Liu and 12 other authors, released on January 8, 2026.

## The Problem

The paper demonstrates that directly applying GRPO (Group Relative Policy Optimization) to normalize distinct rollout reward combinations causes them to collapse into identical advantage values, reducing the resolution of the training signal and resulting in suboptimal convergence and, in some cases, early training failure.

## The Solution

GDPO is a new policy optimization method that resolves these issues by decoupling the normalization of individual rewards, more faithfully preserving their relative differences and enabling more accurate multi-reward optimization, along with substantially improved training stability.

## Key Features

After decoupled group-wise normalization, GDPO applies batch-wise advantage normalization to ensure that the magnitude of advantage does not increase as the number of individual rewards increases.

## Experimental Results

The paper compares GDPO with GRPO across three tasks (tool calling, math reasoning, and coding reasoning), and across all settings, GDPO consistently outperforms GRPO.

The paper is available at: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05242

## DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale

DAPO is an open-source state-of-the-art large-scale RL system that achieves 50 points on AIME 2024 using Qwen2.5-32B base model. The paper was submitted on March 18, 2025, with the latest version revised on May 20, 2025.

**Key Features:**

The system proposes the Decoupled Clip and Dynamic sAmpling Policy Optimization (DAPO) algorithm. Unlike previous works that withhold training details, the researchers introduce four key techniques of their algorithm that make large-scale LLM RL a success.

The four key techniques are: (1) Clip-Higher, which promotes diversity and avoids entropy collapse; (2) Dynamic Sampling, which improves training efficiency and stability; (3) Token-Level Policy Gradient Loss, which is critical in long-CoT RL scenarios; and (4) Overlong Reward Shaping, which reduces reward noise and stabilizes training.

**Performance & Efficiency:**

The system achieves 50 points on AIME 2024 based on Qwen2.5-32B model, outperforming previous state-of-the-art results achieved by DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B (47 points) using 50% training steps.

**Open-Source Contribution:**

The researchers open-source their training code, which is built on the verl framework, along with a carefully curated and processed dataset.

The paper is available on arXiv at **2503.14476**.

Based on the web search results, here's what I found about the paper "Drift: Enhancing LLM Faithfulness in Rationale Generation" from ACL 2025:

## Overview

Drift is a paper by Jiazheng Li, Hanqi Yan, and Yulan He presented at the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL 2025) in Vienna, Austria.

## Main Contribution

The paper proposes a probabilistic inference paradigm that leverages task-specific and lookahead rewards to ensure that LLM-generated rationales are more faithful to model decisions and align better with input context. These rewards are derived from a domain-specific proposal distribution, allowing for optimized sequential Monte Carlo approximations.

## Key Results

Evaluations across three different reasoning tasks show that this method, which allows for controllable generation during inference, improves both accuracy and faithfulness of LLMs. This method offers a promising path towards making LLMs more reliable for reasoning tasks without sacrificing performance.

## Problem Addressed

The paper addresses the issue that LLMs often generate unfaithful explanations, partly because they do not consistently adhere closely to the provided context.

The paper has been published in the proceedings of ACL 2025 and is available on the ACL Anthology.

I found comprehensive information about Dr. GRPO. Here's what the search revealed:

## Dr. GRPO Overview

Dr. GRPO (GRPO Done Right) is a simple modification to eliminate optimization bias in GRPO, leading to better token efficiency.

## The Problem Dr. GRPO Addresses

Dr. GRPO identifies the bias in optimization of GRPO (Shao et al., 2024), which may lead to progressively longer incorrect responses. More specifically, an optimization bias in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) artificially increases response length (especially for incorrect outputs) during training.

## The Solution

Dr. GRPO introduces simple yet significant modifications to address the biases in GRPO (Shao et al., 2024), by removing the length and std normalization terms. The unbiased optimizer effectively prevents the model from generating progressively longer incorrect responses, thereby enhancing token efficiency.

## Results and Performance

Using the unbiased Dr. GRPO algorithm on Qwen2.5-Math-7B with MATH level 3-5 questions achieves state-of-the-art performance with only 27 hours compute on 8× A100 GPUs.

The paper on Dr. GRPO was published as a conference paper at COLM 2025 and is available on arXiv (2503.20783).

## RAFT: Reward rAnked FineTuning for Generative Foundation Model Alignment

**Paper Details:**
- ArXiv ID: 2304.06767, initially published April 13, 2023 by Hanze Dong and 9 other authors
- Most recent version: December 1, 2023

**Key Contribution:**
The paper introduces a framework called Reward rAnked FineTuning (RAFT), designed to align generative models effectively.

**Problem Addressed:**
Generative foundation models are susceptible to implicit biases that can arise from extensive unsupervised training data, which can produce suboptimal samples, skewed outcomes, and unfairness.

**Approach:**
The approach selects high-quality samples using a reward model, discarding those that exhibit undesired behavior, and subsequently enhancing the model by fine-tuning on these filtered samples.

**Results:**
RAFT can effectively improve the model performance in both reward learning and other automated metrics in both large language models and diffusion models.

The paper is available on arXiv and has also been published in the Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR).

## INFUSE: Fine-Grained NLI Faithfulness Evaluation for Diverse Summarisation

INFUSE is a novel approach that uses a variable premise size and simplifies summary sentences into shorter hypotheses. It analyzes NLI based faithfulness evaluation for diverse summarisation tasks, departing from previous studies which focus on single short document summarisation.

### Key Contributions

The paper introduces DiverSumm, a new benchmark comprising long form summarisation (long documents and summaries) and diverse summarisation tasks (e.g., meeting and multi-document summarisation). In experiments, INFUSE obtains superior performance across the different summarisation tasks.

### Publication Details

The paper was published in the Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL 2024, Volume 1: Long Papers) in St. Julian's, Malta, with pages 1701–1722. The authors are Huajian Zhang, Yumo Xu, and Laura Perez-Beltrachini.

The paper and code are available on the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/HJZnlp/infuse) and through the [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-long.102/).

## INFUSE: Fine-Grained NLI Faithfulness Evaluation for Diverse Summarisation

INFUSE is a novel approach that uses a variable premise size and simplifies summary sentences into shorter hypotheses. It analyzes NLI based faithfulness evaluation for diverse summarisation tasks, departing from previous studies which focus on single short document summarisation.

### Key Contributions

The paper introduces DiverSumm, a new benchmark comprising long form summarisation (long documents and summaries) and diverse summarisation tasks (e.g., meeting and multi-document summarisation). In experiments, INFUSE obtains superior performance across the different summarisation tasks.

### Publication Details

The paper was published in the Proceedings of the 18th Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics (EACL 2024, Volume 1: Long Papers) in St. Julian's, Malta, with pages 1701–1722. The authors are Huajian Zhang, Yumo Xu, and Laura Perez-Beltrachini.

The paper and code are available on the [GitHub repository](https://github.com/HJZnlp/infuse) and through the [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2024.eacl-long.102/).

## MO-GRPO Paper Summary

MO-GRPO: Mitigating Reward Hacking of Group Relative Policy Optimization on Multi-Objective Problems is an arXiv paper (2509.22047), with the latest version submitted on January 9, 2026.

### Problem Addressed
The paper identifies that GRPO is vulnerable to reward hacking in multi-objective settings, optimizing only one of the objectives at the cost of the others.

### Solution
MO-GRPO is an extension of GRPO with a simple normalization method to reweight the reward functions automatically according to the variances of their values. MO-GRPO equalizes scales across objectives before aggregation, making optimization less sensitive to reward magnitude mismatch and improving robustness in multi-objective settings.

### Theoretical Contribution
MO-GRPO ensures that all reward functions contribute evenly to the loss function while preserving the order of preferences, eliminating the need for manual tuning of the reward functions' scales.

### Experimental Evaluation
The paper evaluates MO-GRPO in four domains: (i) the multi-armed bandits problem, (ii) simulated control task (Mo-Gymnasium), (iii) machine translation tasks on the WMT benchmark (En-Ja, En-Zh), and (iv) instruction following task. MO-GRPO achieves stable learning by evenly distributing correlations among the components of rewards, outperforming GRPO.

The paper is available on arXiv at https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.22047, with code available on GitHub at https://github.com/CyberAgentAILab/MO-GRPO.
